item.title: Naomi Osaka issues statement as her 2026 season ends after ‘extreme eye-opener’ this year
item.description: Naomi Osaka’s 2026 season came to an end last month in front of a home crowd in Tokyo. The Japanese star played just 13 tournaments this year, including all four Grand Slams and six WTA 1000 events. But following the resurgent second half of her 2025 season, during which she made the semifinals of the US Open and the final of the Canadian Open, Osaka has not quite kicked on in 2026. While she reached the final in Bad Homburg and the quarterfinals of Wimbledon for the first time, the 29-year-old has not been able to rediscover the level that saw her win four Grand Slam titles from 2018 to 2021. Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images Naomi Osaka releases statement on social media about her season In a post on Instagram , Osaka said: “Someone asked me for a season recap haha. This year has been an extreme eye-opener for me. I used to think I needed permission and approval to be myself, that I was weird for the things I wanted to express and create. “Turns out I was wrong, and the more I trusted my ideas and embraced my uniqueness, the happier and more fulfilled I became. This year is dedicated for anyone who feels a little different and is having a hard time navigating it- you’ll find yourself I promise.” Perhaps Osaka’s most impressive run in 2026 came at the Wimbledon championships, a tournament that, historically, she had struggled at. Prior to this season, Osaka had never made it past the third round of the grass court major across five appearances. But this year, Osaka made huge improvements on grass, reaching the final of the Bad Homburg Open without dropping a set. She was forced to retire during the championship match at the WTA 500 event against Karolina Muchova. Osaka’s impressive grass-court form continued into Wimbledon, where she reached the quarterfinals by beating then-world number one Aryna Sabalenka. Osaka was ultimately knocked out of the tournament by Muchova. After her run at Wimbledon, Osaka made the semifinals in Washington and the quarterfinals of the Canadian Open, but was beaten in the fourth round of the US Open by eventual champion Elena Rybakina. Osaka finished the year with an indifferent Asian swing and ended 2026 ranked 17th in the world, one spot lower than where she started the season.

item.title: Erie native Jon Saraceno covered Ali, Tyson and sports' biggest events
item.description: Erie native Jon Saraceno, a former USA TODAY sports columnist and prominent boxing reporter whose investigative work was nominated for a Pulitzer Prize, died Nov. 4 at Cocoa Beach, Florida, after a lengthy illness. He was 69. Shawn Sell, also a former USA TODAY journalist, confirmed her former husband’s death in an email to the Erie Times-News. More: Erie native Louis Bierbauer was Pittsburgh baseball's original Pirate Saraceno graduated from McDowell High School in 1975 and received his bachelor's degree in journalism from Penn State University in 1979. He spent the brunt of his career in that industry with Gannett Media, now USA TODAY Co. Saraceno’s sports assignments began with covering high school basketball games for The Commercial-News in Danville, Illinois. They peaked with USA TODAY assignments that included the Super Bowl, World Series, Indianapolis 500 and Olympic Games. Saraceno was also a USA TODAY sports columnist. His column, Keeping Score, was published up to three days per week. However, boxing is the sport with which Saraceno will be forever linked. Among the elites he covered and interviewed were Mike Tyson, Larry Holmes, Marvelous Marvin Hagler, Sugar Ray Leonard, Larry Holmes, Roberto Duran and Thomas Hearns. None of those encounters, though, meant more to Saraceno than forging a professional and personal relationship with his boyhood hero, Muhammad Ali. Saraceno’s sustained boxing coverage earned the Nat Fleischer Award for his excellence in boxing journalism. The award is named after the boxing historian and 1922 founder of The Ring magazine. Saraceno also received the William Randolph Hearst Investigative Reporting Award and an Associated Press Sports Editors award for his columns and investigative reporting. More: Erie boxing legend Lou Bizzarro, who fought Roberto Duran for a world title, dies at 78 Where to donate Saraceno, besides his former wife, was survived by a son, Sebastiano Saraceno, two nephews, Mark and Eric Saraceno; a niece, Julie Ritzel; two sisters-in-law, Mary Lou Noyer and her husband, Bruce, and Joyce Gunter; and a cousin, Mark Stevens. There were no calling hours or service. Burial was private. Memorial donations can be made to the Muhammad Ali Center, 144 N. 6th St., Louisville, KY 40202; Penn State University’s Bellisario College of Communications, 201 Carnegie Building, University Park, PA 16802; or Lab Rescue LRCP, P.O. item.title: Kerby Joseph ready to roar in return to Lions: 'I'm used to being counted out'
item.description: For everyone who doubted whether he’d play football again, Kerby Joseph insists he never did. Joseph will play his first game in 406 days this Sunday, Nov. 22, when the Detroit Lions host the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Ford Field. He missed the final 12 games last season with a cartilage condition in his knee and spent the first half of this season on the physically unable to perform list. Activated to the 53-man roster Wednesday, Joseph said Friday he’s ready to “crank” when he gets on the field. “I’m used to being counted out, I’m used to being doubted,” Joseph said. “It just doesn’t faze me no more. So even when it happened, I already knew I was going to be back there, even though everybody else thought I wasn’t going to be. But I already knew I was.” Joseph’s future has been a mystery since he first experienced swelling in his knee after a training camp practice last summer. He tried to play through the injury early in the season, but the Lions shut him down last October when the pain became too much to bear. He returned to practice briefly last December and said Friday the team’s decision to put him on injured reserve was the lowest point of his ordeal. “That was the first time I ever in my entire life gave up on something,” Joseph said. “Not totally gave up, but said I couldn’t go. So that was the first time ever, so I didn’t really know how to take that. But I took it with a grain of salt and then I just had a bigger chip on my shoulder ever since.” RELATED: Why Kerby Joseph still looks like a difference maker in practice Joseph bashed internet speculation his injury was career-ending – “Twitter doctors, they don’t know what I’m talking about. How you going to tell me about my body?” he said – but acknowledged Friday how meaningful it will be to play a football game again. Joseph declined to share the lengths he went to get his knee healthy this offseason, saying only, “God gave me the instruments to get back here.” “[This is] something I’ve been working hard all my life to do, and just to be back out here when the odds weren’t looking in my favor is just, man, it’s just amazing to just come out here and play with my teammates again, to play this game I love,” he said. Lions coach Dan Campbell has tried in recent weeks to temper expectations for Joseph’s return, and he did so again Friday cautioning, “there’s going to be a little rust.” “In practice there was rust when he started three weeks ago, and he’s kicked some of that off as we’ve gone here so this’ll be his first game in a minute,” Campbell said. “Don’t expect it to be perfect, but he’s a football player. And I think he’ll do some things, play within the system and be good.” Joseph said he has not experienced any knee pain since he returned to practice, and he said he expects to be the same impact player he was before his injury. “This [stuff] ain’t rusty,” he said. English Premier League giants Chelsea have undergone major ownership changes behind the scenes in recent months, with Todd Boehly and Mark Walter recently selling their shares , amounting to 12.83% each, to Clearlake Capital affiliates. Now, NFL legend Tom Brady has reportedly bought minority shares in the club, according to ESPN. The seven-time Super Bowl champion had sold his 3.3% stake in Championship club Birmingham City earlier this month. Per ESPN, Defense attorney Alex Spiro is part of Brady’s ownership group and helped negotiate the deal. Brady had joined Birmingham’s ownership group as part of Knighthead Capital Management’s 2023 takeover, and also held a position on the advisory board. His departure was previously reported to be intended to help facilitate an investment into the Stamford Bridge team. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Brady is understood to have a strong relationship with Behdad Eghbali, co-founder and managing partner of Clearlake Capital, which now controls 86.5% of Chelsea following Boehly and Walter’s exit. The 49-year-old also holds a 5% minority stake in the NFL’s Las Vegas Raiders, alongside a minority investment in the WNBA’s Las Vegas Aces. Birmingham confirmed his departure while sitting atop the Championship table, having won League One in 2025 following relegation in 2024. Regardless, the transaction comes after Chelsea’s $3.3 billion takeover in 2022, when the consortium led by Clearlake, Boehly and Walter also committed another $2.3 billion in investment. Boehly and Walter reportedly received $1.3 billion combined for their shares in a transaction valuing the football club at approximately $6.7 billion. Chelsea currently sit fifth in the Premier League and have five wins, four losses and one draw from ten games this season thus far. item.title: Nashville SC out to complete MLS Cup-Supporters' Shield history
item.description: Nashville SC out to complete MLS Cup-Supporters' Shield history By Ben Wright NASHVILLE – In Major League Soccer's 31-year history, only eight Supporters’ Shield winners have gone on to win MLS Cup presented by Audi. Nashville SC are looking to become the ninth, starting with Sunday's Round One Best-of-3 Series opener vs. FC Cincinnati (4 pm ET | Apple TV ; FS1, FOX Deportes). The Boys in Gold made history during the regular season, setting league records for points (77), wins (23), home wins (15), goals conceded (25), and fewest losses (3). Add a Concacaf Champions Cup semifinal run in the spring, and they’ve compiled one of the best seasons in recent memory. However, Nashville know that it will all ultimately feel like a disappointment if they don’t complete an MLS Cup-Supporters' Shield double by lifting the Philip F. Anschutz Trophy on Dec. 18. "We were happy to break the record. That was the goal in the end. We achieved it, and now it's almost a new season. A new tournament starts,” club captain Hany Mukhtar said on Tuesday. “We need to be very sharp and locked in to know what is on the line, but also to know that we are the best team ever, and we should have the confidence.” ⚽🏆 ALL FOR THE CUP Every match matters. Don't miss a moment of the Audi 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs. Watch on Apple TV Team of destiny? It’s hard not to look at Nashville and expect them to win it all. By virtue of winning the Shield, they’ll play all but one of their Audi 2026 MLS Cup Playoffs matches at GEODIS Park, including MLS Cup, should they reach it. They’ve been virtually automatic at their home stadium this year, going 15W-0L-2D and outscoring their opponents 48-14. They’re leaning on their experiences winning the US Open Cup in 2025 and making a run to the 2026 Concacaf Champions Cup semifinals, in which they became the first MLS team to ever win at Mexico City’s Estadio Azteca, as tangible proof that they can deliver with everything on the line. “There is a different mindset, but we have shown, last year in Open Cup and this year in the Champions League, that we are capable of knockout situations and having the pressure a little bit on,” said Mukhtar, the 2022 Landon Donovan MLS MVP. “At the end of the day, there's nothing to fear. item.title: Dave Portnoy Threatens to Sue the NY Times For Quoting Him
item.description: Screenshot via Barstool Sports Barstool Sports founder Dave Portnoy threatened legal action against The New York Times on Friday after the newspaper quoted his own public remarks in a story about the disastrous first season of Michigan football coach Kyle Whittingham . Portnoy, a University of Michigan alumnus and die-hard Wolverines fan, took issue with a Friday report by The Athletic , the Times -owned sports outlet, examining how Whittingham’s once-celebrated hiring has turned into a nightmare for the program. “I did not give the @nytimes permission to use an old quote of mine. Please delete or you’ll be hearing from my lawyers,” Portnoy wrote on X. I did not give the @nytimes permission to use an old quote of mine. Please delete or you’ll be hearing from my lawyers pic.twitter.com/VlJQixbVtg — Dave Portnoy (@stoolpresidente) November 20, 2026 The offending quote? Three words Portnoy enthusiastically exclaimed in a video he posted publicly in December 2025, shortly after Michigan hired Whittingham. “Kyle Whittingham! Yes!” Michigan hires Kyle Whittingham and just like that the kings of college football are back on top! What a spectacular hire! I can’t wait to get my hands on some big nasty Samoans! #GoBlue pic.twitter.com/iXX8ZH000k — Dave Portnoy (@stoolpresidente) December 26, 2025 The Athletic’s Austin Meek and Bruce Feldman included the remark near the beginning of their lengthy examination of Michigan’s struggles, highlighting how the hiring initially drew widespread praise from prominent voices in college football. But Michigan has stumbled to a 5-5 record through Whittingham’s first 10 games, with an offense so ineffective that the school fired offensive coordinator Jason Beck after just nine games. The report detailed growing discontent among players, parents and former staffers, including concerns that Whittingham’s efforts to import his Utah coaching philosophy have clashed with Michigan’s established traditions. Portnoy’s legal threat, meanwhile, quickly drew a public fact-check. An X Community Note attached to his post pointed out that the disputed quote came directly from his own publicly available video, which was captioned, “Michigan hires Kyle Whittingham and just like that the kings of college football are back on top! What a spectacular hire!”. “Portnoy’s ‘Kyle Whittingham! Yes!’ quote is from his own public Dec. 2025 X post/video celebrating the hire. News outlets do not require permission to quote public statements by public figures,” the note read. The post Dave Portnoy Threatens to Sue the NY Times For Quoting Him first appeared on Mediaite .

(Photo by Kavin Mistry/MLB Photos via Getty Images) | MLB Photos via Getty Images The deadline for MLB teams to tender contracts to players who are on the 40 man roster but not currently under contract is 4 p.m. Central today. Players who are not tendered a contract by that time will become free agents. This provides one of the nerdy kind of exciting times in the offseason — a meatier, more substantive version of the Rule 5 Draft. We get to speculate as to what arb-eligible players may be cut loose by teams that do not want to risk the player getting a salary in arbitration in excess of what the team thinks the player is worth. We get to see what contracts are announced today, thus learning which players were in danger of being non-tendered if they didn’t agree to a contract before the deadline. And there will be a spate of players who will hit the free agent market and make us say, oh, hey, he’s a free agent, My Favorite Team should try to sign him. Usually that desire for Your Favorite Team to sign said player is dampened once you take a look at his recent performance level and/or injury history, but still, that bit of frisson when you see a name that once was associated with something of value being out there and available is something we can all enjoy in these noisome November nights. Take, for instance, Nolan Gorman. He was the Cardinals’ first round pick in 2018, taken four picks after the Rangers selected Cole Winn. Keith Law actually mocked Gorman to the Rangers in one of his mock drafts that year.* He was a consensus top-100 prospect from 2019-22, and was a consensus top-35 prospect in 2022. In 2023 he put up an 805 OPS with 27 home runs. And he’s reportedly being non-tendered. The Rangers should jump all over him! * In searching to see if I had done a draft preview of Gorman that year, I found this write-up I did in 2019 of someone named Jimmy Lewis. For the life of me, I have no memory of doing this write-up, or of this Jimmy Lewis guy ever existing. Alas, he’s kind of been bad since then. He’s played second base and third base, neither of them well, and after slashing .204/.284/.385 in the 2024-25 seasons, Gorman ended up splitting 2026 between the majors and AAA, slashing .184/.272/.308 in the former and .182/.328/.430 in the latter. item.title: Chris Russo fears entire 2027 MLB season is ‘in jeopardy’
item.description: Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-USA TODAY Sports Less than three months after saying he’s confident there will be a 2027 Major League Baseball season, Christopher “Mad Dog” Russo is worried. We’ve known baseball was heading toward a lockout for about as long as we’ve known the current collective bargaining agreement between MLB and the MLB players was set to expire after the 2026 season. Even while knowing a lengthy lockout was looming, Russo confidently predicted there will be a 2027 MLB season this past September. But we haven’t even made it to the lockout yet, and Russo is already changing his tune. In recent weeks, commissioner Rob Manfred has maintained the owners will not compromise on their desire to institute a salary cap. The players, meanwhile, have refused to even entertain a CBA proposal from the owners that includes a salary cap. And with no room for negotiation on the horizon, Russo expressed doubt about baseball being played in 2027 during an appearance on The Dan Patrick Show on Friday morning. ﻿ “The players are not going to engage in these last proposals,” Russo told Patrick. “Because if they do that, then they’re basically telling you that we’ll deal with the salary cap.” Russo noted this is likely heading to court, with the players possibly seeking to file a disclaimer of interest to dissolve the union, allowing them to pursue antitrust lawsuits against the league. “If they win, there’s going to be an appeal. If they lose their appeal, this could take forever,” Russo continued. “I don’t talk to the owners, but I do believe they’re very committed to getting this done.” There is some precedent for PA’s filing a disclaimer of interest. The NBPA did it during the 2011 NBA lockout, dissolving the union on Nov. 14 before quickly reaching a tentative CBA agreement on Nov. 26. But MLB owners and players seem further apart on an agreement with a salary cap on the line. And Russo insists MLB is in a better position to institute a salary cap now than they were during the strike shortened season in 1994, because currently, they’re a league ran by lawyers. “Unlike ’94 with [Bud] Selig, who wasn’t a lawyer, they got good lawyers. Manfred’s a lawyer. He want to Harvard Law School. Dan Halem, his right hand-hand man went to Cornell… they got that buttoned-up. And I think they feel the union can’t win in court, so as a result of that, the union’s going to have to fight that in court, and so, this is going to take forever. But I do believe, the owners are very, very committed to getting this fixed once and for all.” “I believe it needs to be fixed. That’s my opinion. Some people would disagree, but I think this is going to be a very long, drawn out process,” Russo added. “It’s a long way to go. It’s Nov. 20. I think the ’27 season is in jeopardy. I really do. item.description: SSC Napoli v Udinese Calcio - Serie A - Getty Images Sport Antonio Conte has launched a stinging critique of Manchester United following the club's decision to appoint Mauricio Pochettino as their new permanent manager. The Italian tactician, who was heavily linked with the vacancy at Old Trafford, suggested that the hierarchy's hesitation to hire him reflects a deeper issue within the club. Conte questions United's ambition Conte has hit out at clubs that decide against hiring him , suggesting they are 'frightened of winning' due to his notoriously demanding and intense coaching style. The 57-year-old was widely considered a frontrunner for the Manchester United job following the dismissal of Michael Carrick, but the Premier League giants ultimately chose to appoint former Tottenham and Chelsea boss Pochettino instead. Known for his uncompromising approach and high-intensity tactical drills, Conte has a proven track record of success, having secured five Serie A titles alongside a Premier League trophy during his tenure at Chelsea. However, it appears his reputation for being a volatile and difficult figure to manage may have played a role in United's decision to look elsewhere for their long-term project. 'Manchester United has such a significant history that I find it strange to imagine anyone could be afraid of an approach aimed at restoring the club to its true stature. They last won the league in 2013, under Ferguson. I have immense respect for Sir Alex Ferguson. He has an incredible passion for talking about football,' Conte told Cronache di spogliatoio. item.title: McInnes To Make Changes? | Predicted 4-4-2 Rangers Lineup To Face Motherwell
item.description: McInnes To Make Changes? | Predicted 4-4-2 Rangers Lineup To Face Motherwell Despite their comprehensive win over St Mirren in Paisley, Rangers have dropped points in their recent outings away from home. Another tricky test on the road awaits Derek McInnes’ men, with the Light Blues set for a trip to North Lanarkshire to lock horns with Motherwell on Saturday night. The Well dominated this fixture last season, claiming one win and two draws in four Premiership encounters. However, they lost at Ibrox in September’s reverse tie, and with just one victory in their last nine games, young Swedish boss Alfred Johansson has found his side battling for survival at the wrong end of the league standings. Nevertheless, the Steelmen enjoyed a three-game unbeaten streak before the international break, and it remains to be seen whether the momentum is maintained this weekend. Ivor Pandur has been a shining light between the sticks, as the Croatian custodian made some stellar saves while clinching back-to-back clean sheets against Aberdeen and St Mirren. He must show his supremacy in goal and help his side snatch all three points to keep pace with Old Firm rivals Celtic. GLASGOW, SCOTLAND – DECEMBER 27: Youssef Chermiti of Rangers attempts a shot at goal during the Premier League match between Rangers and Motherwell at Ibrox Stadium on December 27, 2025 in Glasgow, Scotland. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images) Rangers have a stable backline, with Dujon Sterling likely to retain the right-back spot ahead of Kosta Nedeljkovic. Centre-half Ben Godfrey and left-back Tuur Rommens started the campaign as the preferred options, but have lost their place following Olwethu Makhanya and James Penrice’s emergence during Godfrey and Rommens’ brief injury layoffs. They must feature again in their respective roles, and so should Emmanuel Fernandez, who has been a revelation in deep defence since his low-key arrival last year from Peterborough United. Midfield McInnes has found stability in the middle of the park, with Nicolas Raskin and Dan Neil offering the right balance and technicality. Their defensive contribution, box-to-box runs, and link-up play would frustrate the home side in their efforts to dominate the midfield battle. Cammy Devlin and Ross McCrorie remain sidelined, but they have Vanja Dragojevic and Tochi Chukwuani, who could feature from the bench at some point in the second half. Badredine Bouanani has made a positive impact since his late transfer from VfB Stuttgart on a season-long loan. The Algerian should operate from the right, allowing versatile Min-Su Kim to occupy the left midfield role over Findlay Curtis and Djeidi Gassama. Ryan Naderi and Kevin Kelsy have stepped in as the centre-forward pairing amid injuries to Lawrence Shankland and Youssef Chermiti. Bojan Miovski would continue as the understudy to the first-team duo, as he has found his minutes limited high up the pitch.
